Bug_Details:
According to the J2EE specification, an EJB should not have any static fields
with write access. However, static read-only fields are allowed. This ensures proper
behavior especially when instances are distributed by the container on several JREs.
Examples:
public class SomeEJB extends EJBObject implements EJBLocalHome {

    private static int CountA;          // poor, field can be edited

    private static final int CountB;    // preferred, read-only access
}
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by keeping a non-final static field 'CountA' which can be modified across instances, violating the J2EE specification for EJBs.
Trigger_Explanation: The test triggers the bug by calling the showBug method on two different instances of SomeEJB. Since CountA is a static variable, it is shared between instances, causing the second call to showBug to return 2 instead of 1.
